title: A General Framework for Pairs Trading with a Control-Theoretic Point of View

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper presents a control-theoretic framework for pairs trading using an arbitrary mean-reverting spread function of underlying stock prices. Using a staggered sliding window method for parameter estimation (training window of length 40 and trading window of length 5), a threshold-based feedback trading algorithm dynamically adjusts stock holdings based on the spread's deviation from zero relative to a computed threshold.
extraction.universe: Direxion Daily FTSE China Bull 3X ETF (YINN) and Direxion Daily FTSE China Bear 3X ETF (YANG)
key_findings: The proposed control-inspired trading algorithm guarantees positive expected growth in account value for all periods where trading occurs.
Simulations on historical ETF data (YINN and YANG) demonstrate robust gains compared to buy-and-hold strategies while avoiding huge drawdowns.
The algorithm avoids disastrous drawdowns by halting trading when estimated thresholds become excessively high during unfavorable market periods.
extraction.extraction_notes: The paper presents a theoretical framework and visual simulations of account value, but does not explicitly report exact tabular performance numbers such as annualized return or Sharpe ratio in the text.
